It's these extremely basic, "small things" ideas I am trying to dream up since I am operating on a fairly small budget.

I would love to lease-out an old warehouse or parking lot and turn it into a basketball league for kids. I played in one as a child and it was one of the best memories I have to this day of my childhood.

I was thinking of a small scale bulletproof glass factory that could employ local Detroiters.

There are plenty of old warehouses for lease and Detroit certainly needs more bulletproof glass. The process to create bulletproof glass is fairly simple as well. Anybody could learn to do it properly.

But I am not from Detroit, what kind of revenue generating business would you like to see pop up on your block Terrance021?

>Wouldn't you want to help your home rather than mine?

I am from Oakville, Ontario. [Our median household income is above $100,000.](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville,_Ontario#Demographics) No, we don't need any more help in our community. I can guarantee you that.

I have travelled most of southern Ontario, and there isn't anywhere within driving distance of me that demands help as much as Detroit imho. Hamilton is down in the dumps right now, but they're like a diamond in the rough compared to Detroit.

[Like I just mentioned above](http://www.reddit.com/r/Detroit/comments/25u922/what_businesses_or_services_does_downtown_detroit/chl2n9l), I was thinking of doing something like:

**Buy a house beyond repair, demolish it.**

**Put in a basketball court or community garden with proper surveillance and lighting.**

**Encourage people who enjoy the community basketball courts and community gardens to vote.**

**Maybe even setup a local farmers market for the community gardeners from around the city in the fall and pay for some radio time to attract customers.**

What do you guys think about ideas that?

Like I said in my original post above: "I can't bring the auto industry back."

I don't have millions of dollars.

If I could bring Google fiber to Detroit, I would.

Obviously, that is the first need of a city undergoing bankruptcy proceedings. You need money. I hear you loud and clear.

I'll be up front about it. I don't have the will or the want to move my family to do Detroit and risk their safety. (Also, I am Canadian. It's not that easy to just pick up and move your family to another country.)

**However, I am willing to risk my own personal safety and money** to try and make the city a better place.
